turns.text:
The criteria score here is 0.9013 (c:score:0152_0083:criteria), built on a known share of 0.667 (c:score:0152_0083:criteria:known). Four criteria carried it at full membership 1.0: conductor proximity (c:crit:0152_0083:conductor_proximity), fault proximity (c:crit:0152_0083:fault_proximity), mapped graphitic host (c:crit:0152_0083:graphitic_host), and unconformity depth in the window (c:crit:0152_0083:unconformity_depth). Structural density was measured and nearly failed at 0.013 (c:crit:0152_0083:structural_density), and three criteria are unknown (boulder train, lake sediment, lake water) — unmeasured, not failed. The two folklore criteria (conductor strength, EM bright spot) carry weight zero and do not affect the score (c:crit:0152_0083:conductor_strength:weight, c:crit:0152_0083:em_bright_spot:weight).

Is the learned score explained by drilling history here? The evidence says largely not. The effort score for this cell is 0.0338 (c:score:0152_0083:effort) — very low — and the learned score is 0.0245 (c:score:0152_0083:learned), even lower. The cell itself has zero provincial drillhole collars within 2 km (c:cell:0152_0083:holes_n) and no lake-sediment samples (c:cell:0152_0083:sed_samples_n); exploration contact is limited to survey footprints (7 airborne, c:cell:0152_0083:airborne_surveys_n; 7 ground, c:cell:0152_0083:ground_surveys_n) and an earliest drilling year of 2007 within 5 km (c:cell:0152_0083:holes_first_year). So the learned score is low because exploration history is thin here, not high because of it: what is high in this cell is the geology-driven criteria score, not the history-driven one. Grid-wide, the effort model does outscore the geological model under spatial folds (effort ROC-AUC 0.8524, c:metric:effort.spatial.roc_auc), so a low learned score still reflects a history-informed fit — but in this cell the exploration-history signal is near zero and the learned score tracks that.

turns.question: Which single unmeasured criterion would move the score most if it were measured?
turns.text: The sensitivity ranking has a tie at the top: boulder train (radioactive boulders nearby) and lake-sediment uranium would each move the criteria score equally if measured and met. The score now is 0.9013 (c:sens:0152_0083:score_now). If boulder_train were measured and met, the score would be 0.9177, a move of 0.0164, and if measured and not met it would fall to 0.7511 (c:sens:0152_0083:boulder_train:score_if_met, c:sens:0152_0083:boulder_train:delta_if_met, c:sens:0152_0083:boulder_train:score_if_not_met). Lake-sediment uranium is identical: 0.9177 if met, delta 0.0164, 0.7511 if not met (c:sens:0152_0083:lake_sediment_uranium:score_if_met, c:sens:0152_0083:lake_sediment_uranium:delta_if_met, c:sens:0152_0083:lake_sediment_uranium:score_if_not_met). Lake-water uranium ranks third at 0.9103 if met, delta 0.009, 0.8194 if not met (c:sens:0152_0083:lake_water_uranium:score_if_met, c:sens:0152_0083:lake_water_uranium:delta_if_met, c:sens:0152_0083:lake_water_uranium:score_if_not_met). Both tied criteria carry weight 2.0 (c:crit:0152_0083:boulder_train:weight, c:crit:0152_0083:lake_sediment_uranium:weight). The sensitivity tool ranks boulder_train first and lake sediment second only by listing order; the movement it reports is the same for both, so the single most consequential unmeasured criterion is a tie between them. Note also what each outcome does to the known share: measuring either lifts it from 0.667 to 0.8 (c:sens:0152_0083:known_share, c:sens:0152_0083:boulder_train:known_share_after, c:sens:0152_0083:lake_sediment_uranium:known_share_after).
